protocol.admission_rule: ADMIT frame must be fully durable and read-back-valid before any slot work is launched.
protocol.slot_rule: A canonical slot result becomes scientific state only after its complete checksummed SLOT frame is durable. The first durable payload for the deterministic slot event id wins; exact retries are idempotent and conflicting retries are quarantined.
protocol.close_rule: CLOSE is the sole durable block commit marker. The closed row is derived from the admitted plan plus accepted durable slots; absent slots contribute fail-closed score 1. Numerical process/exposure caches are reconstructed from the one deduplicated closed row and are never independent durable truth.
protocol.torn_tail_rule: Recovery accepts only the complete checksummed prefix. A torn final append is ignored. If a durable ADMIT remains active past its deadline, recovery can append a deterministic CLOSE marker; torn slot writes remain missing/fail-closed.
protocol.late_result_rule: A SLOT arriving after CLOSE or after the frozen deadline is ignored and cannot overwrite an earlier accepted result.
protocol.storage_scope: The model covers a single-writer ordered append stream with durable-prefix semantics. It detects a torn/corrupt tail frame but does not claim recovery from arbitrary mutation of earlier already-durable bytes, broken fsync semantics, or reordering by a storage substrate that violates the assumed append contract.

properties_checked: partial ADMIT never creates a planned block; protocol forbids outcome launch until full admission durability
partial SLOT never becomes accepted scientific evidence and therefore remains fail-closed if never retried
partial CLOSE leaves the block active; deterministic recovery CLOSE yields exactly one closed row
conflicting retry for the same deterministic slot event id cannot overwrite the first durable payload
post-close late slot cannot change the closed row
each closed block replays exactly once into the equal-process channel and exactly once into the planned-exposure channel

public_systems_precedent.observed_relevance: SQLite explicitly treats crash consistency as an atomic-commit problem and tests simulated incomplete writes/out-of-order damage. This supports using crash injection as a first-class validation method, but does not prove this role-local protocol under arbitrary filesystems.
WAL commits are represented by a commit-marked frame, providing a systems precedent for separating durable append records from reconstructed database/cache state.

conclusion: Within the tested single-writer durable-prefix model, admission/slot/close write ordering plus deterministic event identities is sufficient to prevent a planned slot from silently disappearing after durable admission, prevent late/conflicting overwrite, and prevent a closed block from being counted twice across the two replay channels under the injected partial-write and retry cases.
not_established: correctness on a storage substrate that can corrupt or reorder already-durable earlier records
multi-writer concurrency without an external serialization/CAS layer
optimality of the framing format or of fsync/checkpoint frequency
production failure probabilities or latency overhead
statistical optimality of the dual-channel tolerances or block-size policy
